items.title: William "Ba Ba" Ridgley Interview, 1959-06-02
items.q: And Mr. George Gates engaged us to play in the airplane.

ctx.x: Here's one other thing I heard once, something about you went up in an airplane.

Did, Friday, June of 1924. Gates, Flying Cycles, used to come from California every summer. We were playing at that time at Francina's Restaurant at Spanish Fort. And Mr. George Gates engaged us to play in the airplane. Let me get that. That was Celestine, William Racely, John Marrero, Simon Marrero, Paul Barnes, and Williton, a fellow by the name of Williton, on drum at that time.
Could you get out the whole band in the plane? No. The plane big enough then? Two of us. Two at a time.

items.title: William "Ba Ba" Ridgley Interview, 1961-04-07
items.q: And Mr. George Gates, the president of that company, told us that we were the first one that played live music in the air, Tuxi the band.

ctx.x: Didn't have a back to it or anything?

No. Well yeah, something like that to keep them falling out. We had a back. That's very good. Things like that. Then when we played in the hour playing on Friday, June of 18, 19 and 24, Gitt's aerial circus used to come here every summer. And Mr. George Gates, the president of that company, told us that we were the first one that played live music in the air, Tuxi the band. Of course there had been piano players and different things like that, records and so on, like you said, but we were the first one to play…
Did you know a fellow named Henry Lambert way back?
